<Task 1 full original text, verbatim, including its Files: and Tests: blocks>

```bash

(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/format.test.mjs)
```

## 3. Identify affected tasks, then stage

Before staging, I list what the repair touched. The repair is unstaged against the already-staged integration.

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --name-only
git -C /workspace/project status --porcelain --untracked-files=all
```

- Affected tasks are those whose `Files:` own a touched path.
- Per the observation, only Task 1's files (`src/parse.mjs` and/or `tests/parse.test.mjs`) are touched, so Task 1 is affected.
- If a Task 2 path appeared, Task 2 would also get its own SR.

Then I stage the repair deliverables:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

- I keep the printed tree SHA as Task 1's SR tree-before.
- A later SR re-review, if any, diffs from this SHA.
- A nonzero exit stops dispatch, and I report the shell error.
